question.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y={e}^{3x}
$$

has the general solution

$$
y(x)=A{e}^{2x}+Bx{e}^{2x}+{e}^{3x},
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y={e}^{3x},\,y(0)=1,\,{y}^{′}(0)=2.
$$
question.worked_solution:
We find the constants $A$ and $B$ by substituting the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(0)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =A{e}^{2(0)}+B(0){e}^{2(0)}+{e}^{3(0)} \\ 1 & =A+1 \\ A & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

- Differentiating $y$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=2A{e}^{2x}+2Bx{e}^{2x}+B{e}^{2x}+3{e}^{3x}.
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(0)=2$ into the derivative we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =2A{e}^{2(0)}+2B(0){e}^{2(0)}+B{e}^{2(0)}+3{e}^{3(0)} \\ 2 & =2A+B+3 \\ -1 & =2A+B \\ -1 & =2(0)+B \\ B & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $A=0$ and $B=-1,$ we have the following solution to the initial value problem:

$$
y=-x{e}^{2x}+{e}^{3x}
$$
